title: Subarrays Distinct Element Sum of Squares I
summary: Given an integer array nums, calculate the sum of the squares of the distinct counts for every possible subarray.
statement: Given an integer array nums, calculate the sum of the squares of the distinct counts for every possible subarray. A subarray is defined as a continuous segment of the array.
constraints: For every nonempty contiguous subarray, count its distinct values.
Square that distinct count and add it to the answer.
Return the total over all subarrays.
hints: Extend the right endpoint one position at a time while maintaining a set of encountered values.
After each extension, add the square of the set size.
Every nonempty subarray has one unique left/right pair and is therefore evaluated exactly once with its exact distinct set.
editorial: Every nonempty subarray has one unique left/right pair and is therefore evaluated exactly once with its exact distinct set.

tests.explanation: The six subarrays have distinct counts 1,2,2,1,2,1; their squares sum to fifteen.
The two length-one subarrays and the full subarray each contribute one.
